chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Hamza, who said:

The Believer mingles his deeds with forbearance; he sits to learn and speaks to understand. He does not narrate his entrusted secrets to his friends, nor does he conceal his testimony from his enemies. He does not do any act of truth for the sake of showing off, nor does he leave it out of shyness. If praised, he fears what they do not know; he seeks forgiveness from Allah for what they do not know. He is not deceived by the words of those who are ignorant of him, and he fears the recording of what he has done.

key_terms.إِحْصَاءَ: Recording or counting (of deeds), referring to divine accounting
key_terms.الْحِلْمُ: Forbearance, patience, and gentleness in conduct
key_terms.حَيَاءٌ: Shyness or modesty, sometimes leading to withholding truth
key_terms.رِيَاءٌ: Showing off, performing deeds for public recognition

ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical characteristics of a believer according to this hadith from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Abu Hamza al-Thumali elucidates the concept of 'hilm' (forbearance) not merely as patience, but as a comprehensive ethical framework governing the believer's interaction with truth and self. It highlights the delicate balance between sincerity (ikhlas) and humility, warning against the pitfalls of riya' (showing off) and haya' (shyness) distorting the performance of duty, while emphasizing the fear of God's accounting over public opinion. This reflects the Shia emphasis on internalizing faith through consistent, mindful action in both private and public spheres.
